exposure: Bacterial pathogens isolated from surgical site infections (SSI)
Antibiotic resistance profiles of these pathogens
outcome: Clinical outcomes of women with post-CS SSI
cohort: The study included 66 women presenting with clinical signs of post-Caesarean section surgical site infection at the largest national maternity hospital in Kampala, Uganda.
finding: Deep wound swabs from post-CS SSI predominantly identified multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens, with Acinetobacter spp., Escherichia coli, and Klebsiella spp. being the most frequent, many of which showed high resistance to third-generation cephalosporins and carbapenems.
followup_time: A median of 22.9 days after birth (12.2 days from CS to diagnosis + 10.7 days of in-patient treatment until discharge)
